results.title: Nebius, CoreWeave stocks surge on short-term AI cloud contracts | Content Fans
highlights:
August 18, 2026

Nebius and CoreWeave stocks rose sharply after they offered short-term cloud contracts to take advantage of the current GPU shortage. These short contracts, lasting three to twelve months, may let providers change prices quickly as AI demand changes, and help customers avoid being locked into longer deals. Analysts suggest customers pay more for these flexible terms to get GPUs now, but this may come with risks like higher renewal costs and less planning security for providers. It appears that this strategy could be a shift for smaller companies to compete with larger cloud providers and may keep prices high as long as GPUs are scarce.

The recent surge in Nebius and CoreWeave stocks is linked to their new strategy of offering short-term AI cloud contracts to capitalize on the ongoing GPU shortage. Investors have responded positively to the move, which involves three- to twelve-month deals that allow the companies to reprice capacity dynamically as AI demand fluctuates (source). This flexible approach signals a competitive shift, positioning these smaller "neoclouds" against hyperscalers who typically favor long-term, multi-year commitments.

...

Nebius and CoreWeave are leveraging short-term contracts to maximize revenue during the current GPU scarcity. This strategy allows them to charge premium rates that reflect immediate market demand, unlike discounted long-term deals. Customers gain flexible access to high-demand hardware, while the providers capitalize on scarcity pricing.

Following the announcement, the market reacted swiftly. Reuters reported an August 12 rally where Nebius stock surged 34% and CoreWeave gained 19% after management emphasized their "pricing power" (link). Industry reports suggest this pricing advantage is significant, with short-term capacity commanding substantially higher rates than longer contracts. Key performance indicators include:

- Nebius: Secured multiple significant AI cloud deals.
- CoreWeave: Increased prices on its H100 clusters in July.

Analysts view this price difference as a premium customers are willing to pay for immediate GPU access without long-term commitments.

...

However, this flexibility is not without risks. Industry analysts caution that customers on short-term deals face significant renewal risk, especially if GPU scarcity continues. For providers, the lack of long-term commitments reduces the predictable revenue streams often required for financing data center expansions. Furthermore, law firm Mayer Brown points to potential migration costs, as even short-term leases can create platform lock-in through specific networking and storage configurations, making it costly for customers to switch providers.

...

The financial results are compelling: Nebius reported that short-term contracts drove a majority of new bookings, while CoreWeave credited these deals for doubling its second-quarter revenue. This success indicates that scarcity pricing is holding firm, even as more H100 and H200 GPUs enter the market. While it remains to be seen how long customers will pay this premium, investors are currently rewarding the strategy of prioritizing high immediate margins over long-term contract stability.

results.title: Nvidia Rubin ja B200: GPU-hinnat 2,25-16 USD/h [2026]
highlights:
Nvidia on aloittanut seuraavan sukupolven Vera Rubin -alustan toimitukset suurimmille pilvijäteille, samaan aikaan kun Blackwell-sukupolven B200-piiri hallitsee edelleen vuokrattavaa tekoälylaskentaa. Tuntihinnat vaihtelevat markkinoilla 2,25 dollarista jopa yli 16 dollariin per GPU, ja ero riippuu siitä, ostaako laskentatehoa hyperskaalaajalta, erikoistuneelta ”neocloud”-toimijalta vai markkinapaikalta. Datakeskusten piirimarkkina on elokuussa 2026 kahden aikakauden välissä: myyty ja saatavilla oleva Blackwell, ja vasta ovelle koputtava Rubin.

...

## B200 hallitsee vielä vuokramarkkinaa

Kun Rubin on vasta tulossa, käytännön ostopäätökset tehdään tänä vuonna Blackwell B200:n ehdoilla. Hinnoittelu on kuitenkin kaikkea muuta kuin yhtenäistä. Usean hintaseurantapalvelun mukaan B200:n tuntihinta liikkuu karkeasti 2,25 dollarista aina yli 16 dollariin per GPU, riippuen siitä onko kyseessä pitkäaikainen varaus, kertavuokraus vai hyperskaalaajan listahinta. Markkinan mediaani asettuu useiden seurantasivustojen mukaan noin 6 dollarin tuntumaan per GPU-tunti.

Hintaerot syntyvät sopimustyypistä. AWS:n p6-b200.48xlarge-instanssi normalisoituna GPU-kohtaiseksi hinnaksi asettuu noin 14,24 dollariin tunnilta, kun taas Google Cloudin a4-highgpu-8g-instanssi nousee jopa noin 16,11 dollariin tunnilta tietyillä alueilla. Nämä ovat hyperskaalaajien listahintoja, jotka ovat tyypillisesti markkinan kalleimmasta päästä. Erikoistuneet neocloud-toimijat, kuten CoreWeave, Nebius ja Lambda, tarjoavat samaa laskentatehoa halvemmalla: CoreWeaven kahdeksan B200:n HGX-noodi asettuu noin 8,60 dollariin per GPU-tunti, Nebius noin 7,15 dollariin ja Lambda noin 6,69 dollariin.

Halvimmasta päästä löytyy vielä enemmän hajontaa. Yksi palveluntarjoaja mainostaa dynaamista kertavuokraushintaa 3,70–3,75 dollaria per GPU-tunti, mikä on elokuussa 2026 yksi julkisesti ilmoitetuista alimmista hinnoista. Pitkäaikaiset, esimerkiksi 36 kuukauden sitoumukset voivat pudottaa hinnan jopa 2,25 dollariin per GPU-tunti, mutta tämä koskee vain suuria, ennalta sovittuja kapasiteettisopimuksia, ei joustavaa kertavuokrausta. Tarjonta on silti edelleen rajallista: useat hintaseurantasivustot huomauttavat, ettei B200-pilvimarkkina ole vieläkään standardoitunut, koska käyttöönotto on kesken. Moni tarjous on sidottu yrityssopimuksiin tai jonotuslistoihin, vaikka tuote on virallisesti yleisesti saatavilla.

...

## Rubin vastaan Blackwell vastaan Hopper: sukupolvien vertailu

Datakeskusten GPU-markkina elää nyt kolmen sukupolven rinnakkaiseloa. Hopper-arkkitehtuuriin perustuvat H100 ja H200 ovat yhä laajasti käytössä erityisesti kustannustietoisemmissa työkuormissa, Blackwell-sukupolven B200 on tämän hetken suorituskykyisin laajasti vuokrattavissa oleva vaihtoehto, ja Rubin edustaa seuraavaa aaltoa, joka on vasta siirtymässä sisäisistä testiklustereista kohti julkista saatavuutta.

Hintaerot sukupolvien välillä ovat selkeitä. Kun B200:n mediaanihinta liikkuu noin 6 dollarin tuntumassa per GPU-tunti, aiemman sukupolven Blackwell B100 asettuu halvemmaksi, noin 3,99–4,19 dollariin tunnilta. H100-instanssit löytyvät markkinapaikoilta usein vieläkin edullisemmin, mikä tekee niistä yhä järkevän valinnan projekteille, joissa Blackwell-tason suorituskykyä ei tarvita. Tämä hintaporrastus näkyy myös H200:n vuokrahinnoissa, jotka liikkuvat useiden lähteiden mukaan noin 3,82–10,60 dollarin haarukassa per GPU-tunti riippuen sopimustyypistä.

Rubin-sukupolven osalta hintoja ei ole vielä julkaistu julkisesti, koska tuote ei ole kaupallisessa myynnissä. Analyytikot odottavat, että ensimmäiset Rubin-pohjaiset klusterit pysyvät suurten teknologiayhtiöiden sisäisessä käytössä ainakin vuoden 2027 alkupuolelle asti, ennen kuin kapasiteettia alkaa valua julkisille pilvialustoille samaan tapaan kuin Blackwellin kanssa tapahtui.

## What changed since 18 August 2026

Re-checked 7 November 2026: the lineup holds. Every pick was re-read on its own pricing page, and these details moved.

| Platform | What moved | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fireworks AI | September 1 GPU increase took effect; "$1 free credits" line gone | H100 $8/hr, B200 $13/hr |
| Archil | Plans restructured around hard caps and monthly minimums | Free, $10 and $500 tiers |
| Modal | Team now includes $100 a month of credit | Team $250 + compute |

| Cast.ai | Homepage headlines 50 to 80 percent lower costs | Still quote-only |
| Replicate | Nothing | H100 $5.49/hr |

...

## The shortlist: token APIs

Fireworks AI charges per token for serverless inference, with usage drawing down prepaid credits and no commitment. For dedicated capacity it bills per GPU-second, with no charge for start-up time. Its pricing page also lists a Reserved Throughput plan with a 99.9 percent uptime term for steady production traffic.

- Serverless: from $0.05 per million input tokens.
- On-demand GPUs: H100 and H200 at $8 an hour, B200 at $13, B300 at $15, GB300 at $20.
- The caveat: every on-demand tier was raised on September 1, 2026 (our August read had the H100 at $7 and the B200 at $10), and region-restricted deployments are priced at 1.5 times.

Together AI hosts a large catalog of open models. It closed an $800 million Series C on July 1, 2026, led by Aramco Ventures, according to its own announcement, which also reports annual bookings above one billion dollars.

- Tokens: MiniMax M3.1 Flash at $0.15 input and $0.60 output per million; Muse Spark Open at $1.25 and $4.25.
- GPU Clusters, on-demand per GPU-hour: H100 $3.99, H200 $5.99, B200 $8.19, B300 $9.99.
- The caveat: separate rate cards for tokens, dedicated endpoints and clusters mean working out the real bill for one workload takes spreadsheet time.

...

Watch the Blackwell rate cards. Fireworks charges $13 an hour for a B200, and Together lists on-demand HGX B200 at $8.19. If that gap closes, or Fireworks cuts its rate, that is reason enough to reopen a contract signed this month.

...

It depends on the model and the mode. Together lists models from $0.15 input and $0.60 output per million tokens, and its on-demand H100 cluster hour is $3.99 against $8 at Fireworks. Fireworks raised every on-demand GPU tier on September 1, 2026, and its serverless rates start at $0.05 per million input tokens. Price your own token mix on both rate cards before choosing.

results.title: Compute Futures Could Pave Way for AI Investment Stability | Octus
highlights:
Silicon Data and CME Group announced a plan to launch on Oct. 5 two compute futures, according to a joint press release from Aug. 11. The futures contracts would be based on the aforementioned forward prices, which Silicon Data already collects.

“Compute futures give the market something it’s never had: a public, tradable reference price for the resource every AI system runs on. Silicon Data’s benchmarks make that price real; CME makes it tradable. Together, that turns compute from something enterprises negotiate blindly into a market they can actually plan around,” Carmen Li, CEO of Silicon data, said in the statement.

The futures contracts will represent a month’s worth of rent for the Nvidia H100 and Nvidia Blackwell B200, respectively, and will be based on Silicon Data’s H100 Rental Index Futures and B200 Rental Index Futures, which measure hourly rental GPU costs. The futures contracts are pending regulatory approval.

results.title: Old hardware is supposed to get cheaper with time. GPUs are breaking that rule. | Piyush Somani
highlights:
The rental price of an Nvidia H100 has climbed to $2.71/hour, up from $1.96 just last November — a nearly 40% jump in under a year, with forward pricing curving even higher into 2027 and 2028.

Baseten recently shared that its cloud provider is raising B200 rental pricing from $2.63/hour to $5.10/hour when the contract renews in October. Nearly double.

And CoreWeave just locked in a contract for Nvidia's A100 - a chip launched in 2020 - running all the way out to 2029, calling the pricing "attractive."

In every other category of infrastructure, the oldest generation is the cheapest one on the shelf. Right now, in GPU capacity, it's the opposite.
